newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CSR, building shares fall on warning.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CSR, building shares fall on warning.

text.p: Shares in building materials group CSR Ltd fell sharply in early Tuesday trade as investors and dealers reacted to the company's warning that first half profitS were likely to fall by about 20 percent.
CSR shares were 10 cents lower at A$4.43 at 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT) on turnover of about 570,000 shares.
The overall share market opened higher, in line with Wall St and continuing the local market's record run.
Another building products bluechip stock, Boral Ltd, was also three cents lower in early trade at A$3.22.
The head of a dealing desk at a European broker said the CSR share price was not expected to fall by much more than 10 cents.
"I would have thought it was a reasonable surprise, just the timing of it," the broker said. "You would have thought they would have probably waited until the interim result came out."
Another broker, in charge of institutional dealing at a large local-owned firm, said the whole building sector was weak and this should not come as a surprise to investors or analysts.
"I don't think CSR has told us anything that we or the market didn't know and that is that the building materials companies are just operating in a very difficult market."

"When you have a company like Boral producing something like only A$50 million in the second half you know things won't be rosy just because it is the first of July (the start of the 1996/97 year)," the broker said.
"That A$50 million was lower than the worst half they had in the last downturn," he said.

Another building company, James Hardie Industries Ltd, was faring much better than its rivals even though it has also forecast lower current year earnings. Hardie shares were two cents higher at A$3.43 at 11.50 a.m. (0150 GMT).
